Brazil Recovers After Major Cyber Attack Shuts Down Payments and Operations Nationwide

Brazilian businesses and consumers are resuming normal activities after a sweeping cyber attack last week crippled the country’s electronic payments network, disrupting commerce, logistics, and energy supply chains across multiple sectors. Among the companies affected was PRIO SA/Brazil, which reported temporary disruptions to its operations as part of the wider outage.

The attack, which began late last Tuesday, targeted the national payment processing backbone used by banks, retailers, logistics firms, and utilities. For nearly 48 hours, point-of-sale transactions, Boleto payments, and instant transfers via Pix experienced intermittent outages. The National Payments Association (APN) estimated transaction volume fell by over 60% during the outage, causing ripple effects for retail, fuel distribution, and port logistics.

PRIO SA/Brazil confirmed Wednesday that it had “experienced temporary constraints in accounts receivable and supplier payments” and had to adjust its shipment schedules. “We have now resumed normal operations following the restoration of national payment services,” a company spokesperson stated.

Telecommunications and energy grids also experienced minor service interruptions as a result of the attack’s impact on automated billing and dispatch systems. The Ministry of Infrastructure said that port operations in Santos, Rio de Janeiro, and Recife faced delays as truckers and customs officials reverted to manual processing.

Brazil’s National Cybersecurity Center said the attack exploited previously unknown vulnerabilities in the payments network software. “This was a highly coordinated intrusion,” said Dr. Fernanda Lopes, chief analyst for cyber resilience at the center. “Our teams worked around the clock with industry partners to contain, neutralize, and patch the affected systems.”

Union leaders praised the rapid response but called for increased investment in cybersecurity. “Our members bore the brunt of this disruption,” said Carlos Silva, president of the National Commerce Workers Union. “Stronger digital infrastructure is essential for economic stability.”

By Monday morning, the APN confirmed 99% of payment services had been restored. Government and industry stakeholders have announced a review of national infrastructure cyber defenses in the wake of the incident.
